newsitem.title: USA: Clinton calls for "national crusade" for education.
newsitem.headline: Clinton calls for "national crusade" for education.

text.p: Making education the top priority of his second term, President Clinton on Tuesday called for a five-year "national crusade" to improve American education standards.

In excerpts from his annual State of the Union speech, prepared for delivery at 9 p.m. EST (0200 GMT Wednesday) to Congress and a national television audience, Clinton also made a strong appeal for racial and ethnic unity.

In a speech that aides expected to last an hour, Clinton proposed $51 billion for education in the budget year beginning next Oct. 1, a 20 percent increase over current spending. Under his program spending would rise to nearly $60 billion a year by 2002 even as other programs are cut to balance the federal budget by that year.

"We must begin a national crusade for education standards -- not federal government standards, but national standards representing what all of our students must know to succeed in the knowledge economy of the 21st Century," Clinton said.

The crusade would involve increasing student access to the Internet and testing of 4th and 8th grade students by 1999 on reading and math skills in an effort to raise U.S. standards, which now lag behind many other industrial countries.
In his appeal for racial harmony, Clinton noted that he had taken the oath of office with his hand on a Bible open to a passage from the prophet Isaiah urging reconciliation.

"I placed my hand on that verse when I took the oath of office, on behalf of all Americans. For no matter what our differences -- in our faiths, our backgrounds, our politics -- we must all be repairers of the breach. We may not share a common past, but surely we have a common future," he said.
